items.title: Review Request for Proposal #20261032, Engineering Service for Matoaka Elementary HVAC Replacement
items.body:
MEETING DATE:
10/6/2026
TOPIC:
Review Request for Proposal #20261032, Engineering Service for Matoaka Elementary HVAC Replacement to
PACE Collaborative, for a Total Cost of $342,513
POLICY ALIGNMENT:
BBA, School Board Powers and Duties
BACKGROUND:
The current HVAC system at Matoaka Elementary was installed in 2007 and has reached the end of its useful
life. Williamsburg-James City County Public Schools solicited sealed proposals from qualified
architecture/engineering firms to produce detailed designs, construction drawings, specifications and contract
documents, and to obtain the necessary related regulatory approvals for replacement of the heating ventilating
and air conditioning (HVAC) system at Matoaka Elementary School. It is the intent of this proposal to result in
the competitive negotiation of a fixed price contract for these services. The successful firm will demonstrate
proven management skills and technical competence in the design of HVAC systems of similar design and
function. It is anticipated that the required design services will include Architectural and Mechanical, Plumbing,
Electrical and Structural Engineering.
The project includes:
 Replacement of four-pipe induction units, make-up air units, hydronic air handling units, split systems,
exhaust fans, air-cooled chillers, boilers, automated HVAC controls, and electrical components
associated with the HVAC system.
 Re-use existing ductwork and piping to the greatest extent possible. Cleaning and sealing of ductwork.
An RFP was issued on May 15, 2026, with a due date of June 12, 2026. Notice of the RFP was posted
Euna/OpenBids and placed on the James City County website.
RATIONALE:
N/A
SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCE(S):
N/A
COST BUDGETED:
The adopted FY26 Capital Improvement Plan includes a total project budget of $480,000. The total cost of the
HVAC Design Fee is $342,513.
ALTERNATIVES:
1. Approve the superintendent’s recommendation.
2. Do not approve the superintendent’s recommendation.



SUPERINTENDENT’S RECOMMENDATION:
The superintendent recommends the board review the Request for Proposal for the Matoaka Elementary
HVAC replacement and be prepared to award the contract to PACE Collaborative, for a total cost of $342,513
at the meeting on October 20, 2026.
DATA SOURCE:
Marcellus Snipes, Senior Director for Operations

items.title: Preschool Centers Design Update
items.body:
MEETING DATE:
10/6/2026
TOPIC:
Preschool Centers Design Update
BACKGROUND:
On May 2, 2023, the Board awarded the architectural design services for two preschool centers to BallouJustice-Upton Architects and PBK for a total cost not to exceed the lessor of 5.5% of Construction Cost or the
budgeted design amount of $3,074,940.
The two 252 student buildings will be constructed on two separate sites (Norge Elementary and Clara Byrd
Baker Elementary Schools). The intent is to replicate the design to use on both sites. A detailed feasibility
study was conducted and provided to the architects. The space will provide classrooms, restrooms, meeting
rooms, offices, a multipurpose space, and administrative spaces for students ages 2-5. The school division
remains committed to a collaborative design process for this project, one that will meet the future needs of
students and best serve the WJCC staff, students, and community for the next 50 years.
The WJCC Standard Operating Procedure for Architectural and Engineering Services ensures the architect will
provide the Board with periodic updates on the progress of the project. Representatives from the firm will
present a final update of the Preschool Centers design and provide an updated project schedule. As a
reminder, the Board received other progress updates on:
September 5, 2023
March 5, 2024
April 9, 2024

items.title: WJCC Profile of an Empowered Learner
items.body:
MEETING DATE:
10/6/2026
TOPIC:
WJCC Profile of an Empowered Learner
BACKGROUND:
As part of the division’s commitment to preparing every student for post-secondary success, WJCC Schools
has developed a Profile of an Empowered Learner that defines the skills and attributes students should
develop throughout their Pre-Kindergarten through Grade 12 experience. Created through a collaborative
design process involving students, educators, families, community members, and other stakeholders, the
Profile identifies five attributes of an empowered learner: Critical Thinker, Collaborative Contributor, Effective
Communicator, Resilient Achiever, and Engaged Citizen. The Profile will provide a shared vision for student
success and help guide instructional practices, learning experiences, professional learning, and opportunities
for students to demonstrate and reflect on their growth. This presentation will provide an overview of the
Profile’s development and introduce the division’s plans for implementation during the 2026–27 school year.
RATIONALE:
The purpose of this presentation is to provide the School Board with an update on the development and
implementation of WJCC’s Profile of an Empowered Learner, a key action within the Superintendent’s
Transition Plan (T1B). Establishing a shared understanding of the knowledge, skills, and dispositions students
need to thrive will help ensure greater coherence across curriculum, instruction, professional learning, and
student experiences. The presentation will highlight how the Profile will move from vision to practice across
WJCC Schools and support intentional opportunities for students to develop, demonstrate, and reflect upon the
five attributes throughout their K–12 experience.

items.title: WJCC United Transition Roadmap
items.body:
MEETING DATE:
10/6/2026
TOPIC:
WJCC United Transition Roadmap
BACKGROUND:
Many WJCC school buildings, particularly at the elementary level, are at or near capacity. Eight of the
division’s nine elementary schools currently use portable classrooms to accommodate student enrollment. At
the same time, the anticipated opening of two new pre-K centers in August 2027 will relocate pre-K programs
currently housed in five elementary schools, creating available instructional space in some buildings while
others are projected to remain at or above capacity. Reviewing attendance zones provides an opportunity to
more effectively utilize available capacity across the division while also considering feeder pattern alignment,
transportation and operational efficiencies, and the effective delivery of programs and services at both the
elementary and secondary levels.
An interdepartmental leadership team has been established to proactively prepare for the 2027-2028 school
year should the School Board approve new attendance boundaries. The team will coordinate a thoughtful
implementation that addresses both operational needs and the human impact of change on students, families,
employees, and school communities.
RATIONALE:
The WJCC United Transition Roadmap will provide a coordinated framework for supporting students, families,
employees, and school communities should new attendance boundaries be approved for the 2027-2028 school
year. Organized around four areas of focus (Student Experience, Employee Experience & Team Transitions,
Family Engagement, and Communications & Logistics), the roadmap will ensure division leadership addresses
both the operational requirements and the human impact of redistricting through proactive planning, clear
communication, intentional engagement, and targeted transition supports.
This presentation will provide a more detailed look at the plan’s Awareness Phase, anticipated for October
through December 2026. Recommended actions and activities associated with this phase are tentative and
contingent upon the School Board’s vote on redistricting. Ongoing updates will be provided as decisions are
finalized and the transition plan continues to evolve.
SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCE(S):
N/A
COST BUDGETED:
N/A
ALTERNATIVES:
N/A
SUPERINTENDENT’S RECOMMENDATION:



N/A
DATA SOURCE:
Alaina Trott, Chief Strategy Officer
Kara Wall, Chief Communications Officer

Eric Swenson
Jill Warren

POLICY ALIGNMENT:
BCF, School Board Committees
BACKGROUND:
Each year the school board appoints citizens to be on the Special Education and Career Ready Advisory
Committees. These committees act in an advisory capacity only. The school board will determine the number
of members to serve on any advisory committee and shall appoint the members of the committee.
Membership on committees shall be in accordance with state and federal laws and regulations and reflects,
whenever possible, the diversity of the community. Members of the WJCC Schools administrative staff shall
serve only as resource persons and liaisons to the advisory committees.
RATIONALE:
Board Policy BCF, School Board Committees, lists the operating procedures to govern the operations of
advisory committees, unless otherwise provided by the school board or by state or federal law or regulations.
Unless prohibited by federal or state law, a minimum of one school board member is appointed to each
committee to represent the board and serve as a consultant to the committee. An advisory committee
appointment term is two years. Members of an advisory committee may be appointed for a second
consecutive two-year term. Members are ineligible to serve for more than two consecutive terms.
Appointments to advisory committees will be made by the first October school board meeting of each year.
The school board may make additional appointments to an advisory committee during the school year. After



committees are formed, any additional applications received will be saved for review and consideration either
in the event of mid-year vacancies, or for possible appointment the following school year.
SPECIAL CIRCUMSTANCE(S):
N/A
COST BUDGETED:
N/A
ALTERNATIVES:
1. Approve the superintendent’s recommendation.
2. Do not approve the superintendent’s recommendation.
SUPERINTENDENT’S RECOMMENDATION:
The superintendent recommends the board approve the appointments to the Career Ready Advisory
Committee for a two-year term ending September 30, 2028 as presented.
DATA SOURCE:
Jessica Walter, Director for School Counseling and College & Career Readiness
Melissa Chai, Career and Technical Education Coordinator
Sherri Thrift, Career Coach
RECOMMENDED ACTION:
Move to approve the appointments to the Career Ready Advisory Committee for a two-year term ending
September 30, 2028 as presented.
